title: Python SDK: SSE -> Async event pipeline ergonomics and streaming chat primitives
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Deliver a small, idiomatic set of Python SDK primitives for handling streaming chat completions (SSE/HTTP2 streaming) and event-first semantics. Goals: (1) make it trivial for application code to consume a stream as an async iterator or push to an event handler; (2) provide robust backpressure and graceful resume/checkpoint APIs; (3) expose developer signals and telemetry hooks; (4) provide clear examples and migration notes for existing consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Provide EventStream and AsyncEventIterator primitives with documented API and examples
BackpressureStrategy support (bounded queue, drop-oldest, block-new) configurable per call
Checkpoint API allowing resume from last-writable event id and integration test covering resume after transient disconnect
Telemetry hooks (latency/queue-length/retry-count) wired to Console tracing API
Type hints and docstrings for all public SDK APIs
At least two integration examples: Flask/FastAPI consumer and an asyncio background worker pattern
progress_updates: 2026-02-10 — Kickoff: scoped primitives after reviewing existing internal patterns (stream router, event bridge). Decision: avoid coupling to internal 'Conductor' — provide minimal thin-shim primitives that are easy to compose.
2026-02-16 — Prototype: implemented AsyncEventIterator + small SSE adapter. Basic API sketch validated with local echo server. Observed bursty input leads to memory growth when consumer is slow.

2026-02-20 — Trade-off discussion: land on configurable bounded queue with three strategies: 'block', 'drop_oldest', 'drop_new'. Chose default 'block' to preserve correctness for chat use-cases. Documented UX implications for web frameworks.
2026-02-27 — Telemetry: added queue-length and per-event processing latency metrics. Wire-up plan approved by Observability team (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3126).

2026-03-03 — Checkpointing: design doc added to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/SSE+Resume+and+Checkpoint+Design. API supports save_checkpoint() -> token and resume(checkpoint_token).
2026-03-06 — Security review: determined no new sensitive data paths; basic guidance for logging PII added to docs.
2026-03-09 — Internal review: PM (Lina Cho) requested clearer migration path for customers using callback-based SDK. Added EventAdapter shim and code example.
2026-03-12 — Integration tests passing on CI for basic resume and backpressure cases. Preparing PR for in-repo RFC and design review.
Next: finalize API names and publish experimental alpha release; solicit early adopter feedback from two internal teams (Console streaming logs and Dedicated autoscaler).
design_decisions: Keep public API small: EventStream, AsyncEventIterator, Checkpointer, BackpressureStrategy, EventHandlerAdapter
Expose both pull (async for evt in stream:) and push (handler callback) patterns — implement push via a supervised task consumer to avoid surprising blocking behavior
Default backpressure strategy = 'block' to avoid silent message loss for chat contexts; allow per-call override
Checkpoint tokens are opaque strings (JWT-like) to avoid coupling to internal cursor format; token encodes last_event_id + model_version + partial_kv_hash
Don't automatically surface retry internals to users; provide sane defaults and telemetry for visibility instead
implementation_notes:
API sketch (informal):

class EventStream:
    def __init__(..., backpressure='block', queue_max=1024): ...
    async def __aiter__(self): yield Event
    async def save_checkpoint(self) -> str: ...
    async def close(self): ...

# push-style adapter
class EventHandlerAdapter:
    def __init__(self, handler: Callable[[Event], Awaitable[None]], ...): ...
    def start(self): ...  # spawns consumer task
    def stop(self): ...

# usage example: async iterator
async with client.stream_chat(..., backpressure='block') as s:
    async for evt in s:
        if evt.type == 'delta':
            buffer.append(evt.delta)
        elif evt.type == 'end':
            await postprocess(buffer)

# usage example: handler
def on_event(evt):
    # quick synchronous filter -> enqueue to worker pool

adapter = EventHandlerAdapter(on_event)
adapter.start()
Avoid exposing internal event envelope changes; maintain stable Event.type and Event.payload fields
Implement tests using a controllable SSE testbench that can pause/resume deliveries to validate backpressure semantics
Make sure GC-friendly: use weakrefs for handler targets and ensure background tasks are cancelled on close
Integrate with existing Python SDK transport layer — reuse HTTP client session and HTTPX/asyncio streams where possible
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: 'block' default may cause surprising application-level latency for users not expecting backpressure. Mitigation: prominent docs, example configs, and liveness metrics exposed via Console.

Risk: resume tokens may become incompatible across runtime versions. Mitigation: include model/runtime version in token and provide migration fallback: server-side best-effort resume or fall back to restart from beginning.
Risk: users writing synchronous handlers could block event pump. Mitigation: provide sync-handler shim that offloads to threadpool and warn in docs. Also include lint rule suggestion in examples.

Risk: performance overhead from queueing for high-throughput batched embedding-like streams. Mitigation: allow 'drop_oldest' and 'drop_new' strategies and recommend non-chat configs for high throughput use-cases.
